head: Term
Meaning
Example
rows: Support analysis
A structured study of practical ways to keep assets and services ready for use.
A team compares repair and supply arrangements before choosing one.
Support
Work and resources that allow an asset to remain usable over time.
Inspection, servicing and replacement components are support activities.
Support system
All people, processes, facilities, tools and agreements contributing to delivery.
An internal team, an outside repair shop and a parts provider work together.
Equipment user
The person or group that relies on the asset to complete a task.
An operations team explains when a machine must be available.
Decision owner
The role authorized to accept a choice or require further analysis.
The owner reviews evidence before an arrangement begins.
Stakeholder
A party affected by, delivering, or providing evidence for a decision.
Users and maintainers describe different constraints.
Stage
A manageable portion of the study workflow, not a mandatory legal phase.
One stage records needs; a later stage compares options.
Requirement
A testable condition or result that a service needs to meet.
A repair must be completed within an agreed period.
Metric
The observation used to measure how well something works.
Hours from a request to a completed repair.
Target
The desired value or state against which results are assessed.
The service reaches an agreed response time.
Gap
The difference between a required result and an observed one.
Only six of the eight needed devices are available.
Outcome
The benefit or operating result the system is expected to deliver.
The needed equipment is ready when work starts.
Options analysis
A comparison of practical choices using relevant and consistent criteria.
A team reviews two repair approaches using the same service measures.
Work breakdown structure
A structured list of distinct activities and their interfaces.
Inspection, parts ordering and component repair are separate entries.
Internal delivery
Work carried out by the organization’s own people or assets.
An in-house team completes regular servicing.
External delivery
Work assigned to a separate provider under a defined arrangement.
A specialist shop repairs a component.
Partner delivery
Work shared with an allied organization under an agreed role.
Two organizations coordinate specialist equipment testing.
Resilience
Ability to keep operating or recover after interruption.
An alternative parts route limits the impact of a closure.
Flexibility
Ability to adjust when demand, conditions or constraints change.
Capacity can increase temporarily during busy periods.
Performance framework
Linked outcomes, measures, owners and review actions.
A service lead reviews delays monthly and investigates causes.
Wider stakeholder effects
Relevant effects beyond direct service delivery, such as inclusion or environmental impact.
A choice is evaluated for accessibility and waste reduction.
Cost-effectiveness
The relationship among useful results, full costs and accepted risks.
The lowest quoted price may not provide the best long-term result.
